name: Randall
description: Street thief of Purewater, raised in a brothel on the Pearl; identical twin of Conall and secretly a son of Baron Hanzo. A nimble, silver-tongued rogue (Deceit 75, Stealth 72, Sleight 71).
narrative: A street thief from Purewater, raised in a brothel on the Pearl and never knowing his parents. Quick, charming and light-fingered, Randall works the canals and alleys with lockpicks, disguises, a grappling hook and a fistful of throwing daggers. He is the identical twin of Conall and, unknown to him, a biological son of Baron Hanzo; his uncanny resemblance to the Baron's son Santo is both an opportunity and a danger.

extras.class_note: Defining Thief skill set: combat style Thief 75, Deceit 75, Stealth 72, Sleight 71, Lockpicking 69, Thieves' Cant 69, Athletics 70. ~5 rogue class skills at 70%+ -> roughly Rogue Rank 2 (Thief); confirm against the Rogue class-skill list if exact rank matters.
abilities: Artful Dodger -- 1 extra Action Point (parry/evade); may use Evade to dodge a melee attack without falling prone (only fall prone on a failure)
Backstab -- may use 'Kill Silently' with surprise
Climb Walls -- ignore 1 grade of difficulty on Athletics to climb
Hide in Shadows -- Perception rolls to spot him are one grade harder
extras.twin: Conall (identical twin brother); both secretly sons of Baron Hanzo; uncanny resemblance to the Baron's son Santo
extras.armor: Studded Leather on all 7 locations (AP 3, ENC 2 each); armor penalty -3
extras.source: Roll20 Classic Fantasy character sheet (And then the Dragons Came campaign)

actor_notes:
Randall
LOOKS: Twenty. Black hair cut by somebody who knew how. A market-stall wardrobe assembled with real care and no money.
CORE: A boy who found out young that his face was worth things and has been living off it ever since, and who is running out of the belief that he is the one doing the choosing.
NATURE: Cheerful, quick, genuinely likeable, and never entirely still. Makes the joke first. Excellent company and completely unreliable about anything that matters, not from malice but because he has never yet been in a room he did not expect to have to leave.
WOUND: He has been four different people this week and only twice on purpose, and he is beginning to find that he cannot always remember which set of answers is the true one.
WANTS: To come out of this conversation with more than he came in with, his face included.
PRESSURE: He gets charming and geographical -- the talk stays light and pleasant while he quietly arranges himself nearer the second way out.
KEY: "I've been someone else four times this week and only twice on purpose."
